newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian trade sees LME copper testing year high.
newsitem.headline: Asian trade sees LME copper testing year high.

text.p: Copper prices are likely to test the year high of US2,440 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday with brisk buying seen from Japanese customers after their Golden Week holidays, traders said.

"I think it will test $2,450 (a tonne)," a senior dealer for a European metal trading company told Reuters. "The Japanese are buying copper and aluminium. They need to stock up because they just finished their holidays."
LME metal brokers Brandeis said the market closed well on Monday and was now taking aim at "the next band of resistance at $2,420 and this year's high at $2,440".
"The technical indicators are rising in confirmation of the market's recent strength with good support now available at $2,400 and extending towards $2,375," Brandeis added.
A dealer for a Japanese trading house said the rise of the yen, which hit a high of 117.50 to the dollar yesterday, also triggered robust buying by Japanese end-users.
Buying slowed in Asian trade after the yen slipped back to around 119.50 to the dollar, traders said.
"If metal prices break lower and the yen resumes its climb, you'll see a resurgence of buying by the Japanese," the dealer said. "The people in Japan are now watching the market."
Three-month copper was seen by the trade at 0300 GMT at $2,415/20 a tonne, up from the kerb close of $2,409 and slightly higher than the late quote on the LME on Monday of $2,416/18.
But the general manager of a Japanese metal trading house in Singapore said copper may be vulnerable to bouts of profit taking later on Tuesday and over the next few days.
"The increase of copper and the rest of the metal complex has been too fast. Prices may drop down as a result," he said. "China is not selling in the market. In fact, it's been quiet."
Another trader said there would be a correction in copper prices, but doubted it would happen when the market opened later on Tuesday.
"I do see a correction, but not today. Copper should go up to $2,430 or higher. It still has some strength on the upside," he said.
While most Far East dealers were optimistic about copper's strength, there were doubts whether aluminium can follow the red metal higher.
"I think aluminium may stall soon," one trader said.

Brandeis said the charts "indicate that there is indecision at the higher numbers. A close above resistance at $1,680 would have been more positive and the market could be due for a small correction with support seen around $1,660 and then $1,640."
Three month aluminium closed on Monday on the LME at $1,670 a tonne and was seen in Asian trade at 0300 GMT indicated higher at $1,670/74 a tonne.

Copper stocks are expected to dip by 300-1,000 tonnes when the LME stocks report comes out at 0800 GMT. Aluminium inventories, on the other hand, were expected to fall by 500-1,000 tonnes, dealers said.
